questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Michelle Obama's UK visit and her message about empowerment
The history of the role of First Lady in the White House
How American presidents and their wives are chosen
Why schools in London are better than schools in the US
questions.why: They talk about Michelle Obama's UK visit to talk about her life, and her message about empowerment.

questions.q: Why was Michelle Obama in the UK?
options: To open a new school
To meet the Prime Minister
To talk about her life and her new book
To start her own political campaign for the next election
questions.why: Rob says she has just published her autobiography and has been talking in the UK about her life.

questions.q: Where did she go that she had visited before?
options: A university in Oxford
A hospital in south London
The BBC studios
A school in north London
questions.why: The BBC report says Mrs Obama revisited a school in north London.

questions.q: What was special about that place for her?
options: It was where she was first inspired to focus on education
It was where she first met her husband, Barack Obama
It was where she wrote her book
It was the school where she studied as a young child
questions.why: She says it was where she was first inspired to focus on education as First Lady.

questions.q: What feeling did Michelle Obama speak openly about?
options: Anger at the media
A feeling that she didn't deserve her position
Sadness at having to leave the White House after eight years
Fear of speaking in public
questions.why: Dan says she spoke about feeling she didn't belong and didn't deserve her position.

questions.q: How does Dan react to the idea of imposter syndrome?
options: He says it is not a real problem
He says only famous people have it
He says he has the feeling all the time
He says he has never heard of it
questions.why: Dan says 'I get that feeling all the time!'

questions.q: According to Rob, what usually causes imposter syndrome?
options: Being genuinely bad at your job
Working too many hours without enough rest or holidays
Having a famous partner
Low confidence or how society labels us
questions.why: Rob says it isn't justified; it's more a lack of confidence or the way society labels us.

questions.q: What mistake does Michelle Obama say people often make?
options: Thinking that education is not important
Thinking working-class people are less gifted
Trusting politicians too much
Believing that real talent can never be learned or taught
questions.why: She says we assume working-class folks are not highly gifted in their own right.
